alerts.title: Untreated hypothyroidism mimics DTG weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has TSH 12.4 mIU/L (target below 4.5) with low Free T4, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed ankle reflexes, constipation, cold intolerance, and tiredness — classic untreated hypothyroidism. She admits often forgetting her levothyroxine. The clinician attributes 9 kg weight gain to DTG and plans to switch, but hypothyroidism is a well-recognised cause of weight gain, fatigue, and cold intolerance. Guidelines list abnormal weight gain as a DTG side effect, so DTG may contribute. However, the temporal relationship between poor levothyroxine adherence and weight gain, plus the severity of hypothyroid signs, strongly suggests inadequate thyroid replacement is the primary driver. Switching DTG without first correcting hypothyroidism risks unnecessary ART change with no resolution of symptoms.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise levothyroxine adherence and dose before considering DTG switch. Recheck TSH after 6–8 weeks of consistent dosing. Address weight gain only if hypothyroidism corrected and symptoms persist.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycaemia risk: BMI 33 warrants glucose monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines require assessing hyperglycaemia risk before DTG use, with BMI ≥25 kg/m² as a risk factor. This patient has BMI 33, placing her at risk. Guidelines state fasting glucose >6.95 mmol/L is high and contraindicates DTG initiation or transition. Her fasting glucose is 5.6 mmol/L, below that threshold, so DTG is not contraindicated on glycaemic grounds currently. However, guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after DTG transition. She transitioned in January 2023 and has only one glucose result recorded, representing a monitoring gap. Her weight gain further increases metabolic risk over time.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue DTG if clinically appropriate but ensure fasting glucose is monitored at least every 3 months during the first year and periodically thereafter given ongoing BMI ≥25.

alerts.title: Elevated lipids with BMI 33 and DTG weight gain
alerts.message: Patient has LDL 4.2 mmol/L, total cholesterol 6.4 mmol/L, and triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L, all elevated. DTG is associated with abnormal weight gain, and this patient has gained 12 kg since starting TLD three years ago, now at BMI 33. The dyslipidaemia may be partly driven by DTG-associated weight gain, but untreated hypothyroidism is also a recognised cause of secondary hyperlipidaemia and is currently uncontrolled (TSH 12.4). TDF can have a modest lipid-lowering effect, partially offsetting this. The compounding of obesity, hypothyroidism, and possible DTG metabolic effects creates cumulative cardiovascular risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Correct hypothyroidism first, then reassess lipids. If dyslipidaemia persists, evaluate cardiovascular risk and consider dietary intervention or lipid-lowering therapy per guidelines.
